title: Daily Debrief — Thursday Nov 5, 2026
html:
Headline: The AI trade cracked, and SPY fell back to its 200-day.

This was the worst day for stocks since April 2025. Most of the damage hit the AI names, and SPY closed right at its low.

The one thing

SPY has one more floor at $722–727, where the 200-day sits. If it holds, the uptrend is bruised, not broken. A close below it means we sit in cash.

SPY fell 4.4% to $733.00 and closed at its low. That usually means sellers aren't finished. The trigger was the Democrats' midterm sweep. Investors fear new limits on AI data-center building, and one UBS estimate says about 30% of the data centers planned for 2028 are at risk. The chip index (SOX) fell 12.3%, its worst day since March 2020. The Nasdaq is in a correction, and the VIX jumped about 70% to 28.18. Airbnb beat and raised after the close and rose about 11% in late trading. Oil: WTI $90.96 (+3.2%) after an 8% drop Wednesday. Odds of a December hike fell to about 70% from 83% (Fed Tracker, Federal Reserve).

SPY levels

  • Record high (Oct 6): $781.62
  • Ceiling: $765–766 (20- and 50-day averages)
  • Old floor, now a ceiling: $750–752 (Oct 30 low, 0.786 extension)
  • First test up: $743–745 (23.6% of the big run, 1.0 extension, and 78.6% of the 60-day swing)
  • Now: $733.00. Today's low of $732.71 landed on the 1.382 extension at $732.44 (Oct 6 high → Oct 30 low → Nov 4 high)
  • The line that matters: $722–727 (200-day $727.39, 1.618 extension $725.06, 38.2% of the Mar 30 → Oct 6 run $722.21)
  • Next stop: $713 (2.0 extension)
  • Deep floor: $701–704 (50% of the big run, 2.382 extension)

How I read it: SPY is still in an uptrend, and RSI 34 matches your tested edge setup. But QQQ, SMH and NVDA are already below their 200-day. A move back above $744 that holds means buyers are back. A close below $722 means stop looking for calls.

Your names

  • NVDA $181.60 (−9.3%) — Avoid. 11% below its 200-day ($204.38). Don't chase puts after the crash. A bounce that fails under $194–195 is the better put entry. Earnings Nov 17.
  • HLT $369.64 (−1.8%) — Ready on trigger. New record at $381.34. The low of $365.87 held inside the $364.50–368.50 retest zone. Enter after the first 30 minutes if it holds above $365.87 and trades back over $370. Stop on a close below $359.41.
  • DAL $85.36 / RCL $322.73 — Wait. DAL held its $83 stop, and a close above $88 re-arms the call. RCL broke $318 intraday, so that plan is void. A fresh setup needs a hold above $310.
  • PLTR $154.99 (−9.7%) — Wait. Sits on its 200-day ($153.56) with RSI 25, so the edge setup is there on paper. Only consider a call after a green close above $160. A close below $150 means it failed.
  • TSLA $343.69 (−10.8%) — Wait for the bounce. Downtrend with RSI 36. The put setup needs a rally toward $372–384 that stalls.

Lesson: the 200-day average

The 200-day is the average close of the last 200 trading days, about 10 months, and it shows the big trend. SPY is still 0.8% above its 200-day ($733.00 vs $727.39). The chip ETF SMH is 14% below its own ($447.73 vs $521.45). Above it, dips are usually buying chances; below it, protect cash. Two closes below, or a failed retest from underneath, would confirm the break.

Plays on deck (Options Playbook)

  1. SPY Dec 18 $765 call, about $622, delta 0.24. Enter only after SPY tests $722–727 and holds, or closes back above $744. Exit on a close below $722. Targets $751, then $765.
  2. HLT Dec 18 $390 call, about $575 (bid $4.80 / ask $6.70), delta 0.38. Enter after the first 30 minutes if it holds above $365.87 and trades back over $370. Exit on a close below $359.41. Targets $381, then $395.
  3. DAL Dec 18 $85 call, about $578, delta 0.54. Enter on a close above $88. Exit on a close below $83. Targets $91.95, then $95.18.

Skip: buying puts on NVDA, AMD, MU or SMH after they tripled today, contracts with delta under 0.20, and holding anything through the 8:30 jobs report on a hunch.

Homework

  1. Mark SPY's $727 and $744 levels. After the jobs report, note which one SPY moves toward first, and whether Friday closes above $733.
  2. Measure how far NVDA and SMH sit below their 200-day lines. If that gap shrinks while SPY holds, the selling is calming down.

Question: Your edge says "buy SPY," but the chip leaders are below their 200-day. Which of those facts would you trust more tomorrow, and what one price would settle it?
